milestone: Personal Experience Host Here Dropdown — By-Design Scoping, Now Explained On-Screen
slice: A real, confirmed report -- 'i have added new scene to the world but the experience is not getting the other scene name in dropdown' -- turned out to be exactly-correct, documented Personal-lifecycle scoping (Builder V3 Canon Alignment Sprint's own Canon Decision #6/#8: a Personal Experience is permanently scoped to the one Scene it was graduated into, and can only reach a different Scene by first Graduating to Public) rather than a bug, but with zero on-screen signal to tell the two apart it read exactly like a bug. Investigated via a comprehensive, real-UI-driven Playwright reproduction (ProjectModel.scenes() confirmed to always reflect a freshly-added Scene with zero caching; a Public Experience's Host Here dropdown confirmed to correctly and immediately show a newly-added Scene; a Personal Experience's own dropdown confirmed to correctly and deliberately show ONLY its own scopeSceneId, never any other Scene including a brand-new one) before touching any code. Fixed by adding a clarifying disclosure note to _renderExperienceAttachPicker(exp) in worldBuilderApp.js -- shown only for a Personal Experience in a World that genuinely has other Scenes it can't reach (never for a single-Scene World, where the distinction is moot) -- naming the real reason and pointing directly at the existing Graduate-to-Public button as the actual way to host it elsewhere. Verified via a new, comprehensive Playwright suite (14/14 assertions, zero console errors) driving the real UI end to end: Create New World -> Blank template -> add Scene A -> seed a Public and a Personal Experience -> confirm the Public dropdown's pre-Scene-B state -> add Scene B via the real Scenes strip -> confirm the Public dropdown now offers both scenes -> confirm the Personal dropdown still correctly offers only its own scoped scene -> confirm the new disclosure note renders. Two pre-existing scratch regression scripts (verify_experiences_dead_end.js, verify_host_here_redraw.js) were confirmed via a git-stash A/B to already hang identically on the unmodified codebase -- both predate the Mandatory Sign-In gate and never mock ThemeRepositoryClient, unrelated to this fix. Both goldenBuild.js suites (World Builder v1 and v2) pass unchanged. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Creator Governing Rules change; confined to tools/world-builder-v2/js/worldBuilderApp.js.
